name: Lalah Hathaway
notes: The lane's jazz-harmony specialist, windowed to the neo-soul-facing 2004–2017 era the entry names rather than to her whole career. The research calls this "the most extension-heavy vocabulary in this section — m11, maj7#11, altered dominants, and reharmonisation of the same melody on each repeat; keys cluster on the flat side (E♭, A♭, B♭, D♭)", so the ninth weight is the highest of any model here, triads all but vanish, `susSubstitutionProb` covers the altered colours and the keys are the flat-side ones. The kit is "jazz-fusion with a light, swung 16th feel, ghost notes throughout, ride-led verses and a snare that decorates rather than states the backbeat" — which is the highest ghost probability in the section, filling all eight 16th positions at low velocity, against a quiet hat and a ride lane that outruns it. The load-bearing vocal claim is register and placement: "a very low, dark contralto placed in the male tenor range, sung at low volume with almost no vibrato, plus deliberate chord-tone-not-root note choices so the vocal is an inner voice of the harmony" — hence the lowest melodic ceiling in this batch, a legato articulation, a very high `chordToneBias` and the color-tone set that keeps it off the root. Bass is "electric or upright with a soloistic role, wide register, and chord-tone-heavy lines that move with the reharmonisation", so its root probability is 0.24 and it climbs to 49 with the chord voicing lifted to 50. ⚠ `session.keys` is part-sourced, part-INFERRED: the entry names four flat-side centres — "keys cluster on the flat side (E♭, A♭, B♭, D♭)" — without qualifying any of them as major or minor, so those four are read from that line while the two minor forms, E♭ minor and B♭ minor, are this author's reading of the entry's m11-first vocabulary rather than keys the research names. ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are every drum number and every melody figure; the research marks the tempo and drum detail as inference and [LOW-CONF]. ⚠ The half-time/double-time feel switches the entry names are not encoded — a single model states one placement.
